topic: Existence of complete mappings of Brauer and partial Brauer monoids
title: Rank-ideal consequences of Dong's solution to the Brauer complete-mapping problem of Araújo, Bentz, Cameron, Hendrey and Kinyon

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We give a rank-ideal consequence and a rankwise proof of Horace Dong's September 2026 solution (Theorem 1.1; version 2, October 2026) to Araújo, Bentz, Cameron, Hendrey and Kinyon's Complete Mappings of Semigroups, arXiv:2608.25092v1, Section 15, Problem 15.11, printed page 61: the Brauer and partial Brauer monoids of positive degree n admit complete mappings exactly when n=1 or n>=4. Every proper Brauer principal factor admits one; the sole partial Brauer exception is the rank-two factor of PB_3, as Dong also proved. We derive the exact existence criterion for every nonempty rank ideal, including degrees two and three. The proof uses adjacent-subset pairings, signed sandwich transversals and rank preservation. Existence does not enumerate individual complete mappings.
summary: A rankwise exposition of Dong's existence theorem, with complete rank-ideal criteria, rank constraints, an identity-sandwich criterion, and a parametrization of minimal-factor mappings.

posing_source.scope: All positive-degree whole monoids and all proper principal factors; minimal-factor enumeration

verification.written_proof: Whole-monoid classification, all proper factors, full rank-ideal criteria, rank preservation, identity-sandwich criterion, minimal-factor parametrization
verification.finite_checks: verify.py: original 1928 subsets, parity through degree 40, 72 S3 sign-fibre cases, 76856 factor products, counts through degree four; also nine small rank-zero/rank-one classes, all 324 PB_3 rank-two products, eight identity-sandwich cases, and all 24 permutations of the two-by-two rectangular band (16 complete mappings)
verification.lean_scope: The declaration result states whole-monoid equivalences and existence of the two source monoid structures; it does not state the rank-ideal or enumeration corollaries
